questions.architecture: Original query and trusted scope -> constrained rewrite -> preservation checks -> original/variant retrieval -> fusion and rerank -> intent-faithful answer
questions.metrics: Constraint-preservation accuracy, retrieval relevance, semantic-drift rate, clarification quality and end-task correctness.
questions.tradeoffs: Multiple variants increase recall, cost and latency. Use rewriting selectively and keep a reliable baseline path for cases where transformation is unnecessary.
followups: Can RRF detect that the rewrite changed intent?
No. RRF combines ranks; it does not establish semantic fidelity. Validate query meaning and evidence separately.
Should conversation history always be included?
Use relevant permitted history with explicit state. Stale or untrusted history can introduce the wrong entity or outdated constraint.

quiz.prompt: A rewrite drops the word 'not' from a policy question. Which metric catches the central problem?
options: Intent and constraint-preservation accuracy.
Only vector index disk size.
Only total number of returned chunks.
Only token streaming speed.

questions.title: Calculate reciprocal rank fusion and distinguish it from score averaging.
questions.simple: RRF gives a result credit for appearing near the top of several ranked lists. It uses rank positions rather than assuming different retrieval scores share one scale.
questions.technical: For document d, RRF(d)=sum_r 1/(k+rank_r(d)), with optional deliberate weights. A result absent from a list contributes zero for that list. The constant controls how sharply high ranks dominate; its optimal value depends on the retrieval task. Deduplicate by stable identity and preserve permission filters before fusion and delivery.
questions.formula:
RRF(d) = sum_r 1/(k + rank_r(d))
k=60
A ranks [1,10]: 1/61 + 1/70 = 0.03068
B ranks [3,3]: 2/63 = 0.03175
B outranks A in this example.
questions.example: A strong keyword hit at rank 1 may lose to an item consistently near the top of both keyword and vector lists. This is a rank-combination choice, not proof the winning passage answers the question.
followups: Why not average raw BM25 and cosine scores?
Their scales and distributions can differ. Calibrated/normalized weighted score fusion is possible, but a naive arithmetic mean can let one score scale dominate.
Does RRF eliminate reranking?
No. It supplies a candidate ordering. A relevance reranker and evidence evaluation can still improve precision, with added latency and model cost.

quiz.prompt: With k=60, A ranks [1,10] and B ranks [3,3]. Which has the higher RRF score?
options: B: about 0.03175 versus A's 0.03068.
A must win because one list places it first.
They tie because there are two lists.
RRF requires the raw cosine scores before it can be computed.

questions.title: Scenario: A multi-agent workflow is waiting for human approval. Is it stuck?
questions.simple: A deliberately paused workflow is different from a failed or looping workflow. Its status should explain what it is waiting for and how it can safely resume.
questions.technical: Represent running, awaiting approval, retrying, failed, cancelled and completed states explicitly. Store a durable checkpoint, authorized approver identity, expiry and operation intent. On resume, recheck current permissions and data freshness; a checkpoint does not preserve authorization forever. Apply separate deadlines for active computation and business approval windows.
questions.example: An expense agent has prepared a refund but waits for an authorized approver. Restarting it with a new run ID can create a duplicate intent; the UI should show the existing pending operation and approval controls.
questions.architecture: Validated intent -> checkpoint -> explicit approval-wait state -> authorized approval/expiry -> permission recheck -> idempotent effect -> terminal result
questions.metrics: Active-step timeout rate, approval wait age, resume success, duplicate effects and unauthorized approval attempts.
questions.tradeoffs: Long approvals require state/version retention and revocation handling. Automatically approving after a timeout improves throughput only by discarding the intended control.
followups: What if the approver's role changed?
Check current authorization at approval/resume. A previously issued notification is not permanent permission.
What should a watchdog restart?
Only a classified recoverable execution failure under an idempotent policy, not every run with no recent tokens or one awaiting approval.

quiz.prompt: An agent is paused at a required human approval. What should monitoring show?
options: An explicit awaiting-approval state with age, approver scope and resume rules.
A crashed state that must restart with a new operation ID.
Automatic approval after any short model timeout.
Completed because planning finished.

questions.title: Scenario: Two agents disagree and a critic keeps asking for another revision. How do you terminate?
questions.simple: More discussion is not always more progress. Define what a valid result is, how many revisions are allowed and when disagreement should be escalated.
questions.technical: Use typed acceptance checks, bounded rounds, per-step and total cost/deadline budgets, explicit unresolved outcomes and durable evidence. Compare artifact changes rather than counting messages. Prefer a deterministic validator for machine-checkable requirements; model critics can share the generator's biases and cannot prove correctness by agreement.
questions.example: A generator and reviewer repeat the same proposed schema change for ten rounds. After the configured two failed correction rounds, return the validation failures and route to a human rather than consume the remaining budget silently.
questions.architecture: Task contract -> worker draft -> deterministic checks and bounded critique -> progress test -> accept, clarify or escalate -> terminal state
questions.metrics: Task success, rounds per success, repeated-state rate, validator failure rate, escalation quality and cost per accepted artifact.
questions.tradeoffs: Tight budgets may terminate solvable tasks; loose budgets increase latency and spend. Tune on difficult cases and preserve an explicit partial-result status.
followups: Does majority voting by three agents guarantee correctness?
No. Correlated models can agree on the same error. Use independent evidence and task-appropriate validation.
What counts as progress?
A relevant artifact change or satisfied requirement, not just new wording. Record failed constraints and compare outputs against them.

quiz.prompt: A critic sends the same artifact back repeatedly. What is a robust termination policy?
options: Bounded rounds, explicit acceptance checks and escalation on no progress.
Continue until all agents sound confident.
Increase every agent's temperature indefinitely.
Remove all validation to force completion.
